 ORDER

These Misc. Appeals under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, are filed by the claimants and Insurance Company, respectively, being aggrieved of award dated 08.03.2019, passed by learned Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Harda (M.P.), in MACC No.42/2017.

2. The ground on which appeal is filed by the claimants is that deceased is survived by four legal heirs and, therefore, 1/4th deduction should have been made, whereas, Tribunal has made only 1/3rd deduction.
3. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company, in his turn, submits that it is a case of false implication.
Reading from Ex.D/3, it is submitted that Ex.D/3 is the document showing that dead body was brought by an unknown person, namely, Sheikh Sajid S/o Sheikh Yasik.

It is submitted that if witness is Jugal Kishore and Om Prakash would have been eye witnesses and would have been travelling with the deceased, then they would have brought the dead body to the police authorities or the hospital concerned.
There is delay of six days in lodging the FIR.

4. After hearing learned counsel for the parties, as far as the ground raised by the appellant-Insurance Company is concerned, there is no suggestion in the cross-examination of Om Prakash Marksule that he was not available at the place of the incident.

On the contrary, his presence has been established in the cross-examination by giving him suggestion that at the time of Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Smt. Shweta Pawar on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93209278/
3 accident, deceased Devendra and this witness were returning back after consuming liquor and mutton.

entities.text: Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Smt. Shweta Pawar on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This suggestion fortifies the belief of the non-applicants that deceased was travelling along with Devendra.

Thus, kind of suggestion in the hands of the counsel for non-applicants which helps in fortifying the claims of claimants and the evidence of witnesses cannot be taken to advantage by the counsel for non-applicants/appellants.

5. Delay of six days is inconsequential, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and also in view of the law laid down by Supreme Court in Ravi Vs. Badri Narayan and others [(2011) 4 SCC 693).

sentences.text:
Thus, appeal filed by the Insurance Company (Misc. Appeal No.3130/2019) is, hereby,
dismissed.

6. As far as Misc. Appeal No.38/2021, filed by claimants is concerned, learned Tribunal has considered income of the deceased at Rs.28,505/- (Rupees Twenty Eight Thousand, Five Hundred and Five) per month or Rs.3,42,060/- (Rupees Three Lacs, Forty Two Thousand and Sixty) per annum.

Tribunal has added 30% towards the future prospects and then made 1/3rd deduction,
which should be actually 1/4th and then after making deduction when multiplier of 14 as applied by the Tribunal, is applied, then total pecuniary compensation will come out to Rs.46,69,119/- (Rupees Forty Six Lacs, Sixty Nine Thousand, One Hundred and Nineteen) in place of Rs.41,71,079/-
(Rupees Forty One Lacs, Seventy One Thousand and Seventy Nine).
7.
Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.4,98,040/- (Rupees Four Lacs, Ninety Eight Thousand and Forty).

Since Court fees has been paid on the enhanced amount on 13.10.2022, this enhanced amount of Rs.Rs.4,98,040/- (Rupees Four Lacs, Ninety Eight Thousand and Forty), will carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of payment of Court fees i.e. 13.10.2022, till the date of actual payment.
Other terms and conditions of the award shall remain intact.
8. This additional amount will remain invested in a monthly scheme of an Indian Post Office/Nationalised Bank in the joint name of the claimants for a period of ten years.

They will use the monthly interest incurred from the fixed deposit for their well being and survival but the principal amount shall not be disbursed to them for the aforesaid period without leave of this Court.
9. In above terms, appeals are disposed of.
10. Record of Claims Tribunal be sent back.
(VIVEK AGARWAL) JUDGE A.Praj.
